# TeleCrypt.io Storage CLI

> End-to-end encrypted Matrix file storage and sharing, distributed only as
> exact GitHub Release archives. The command namespace is `telecrypt-io storage`.

## Installation

```bash
npm install -g https://github.com/TeleCrypt-io/storage-cli/releases/download/storage-cli-vX.Y.Z/storage-cli-vX.Y.Z.tgz
```

Replace `X.Y.Z` with an existing exact release. The archive is fetched from
GitHub Releases, not the NPM registry.

## Authentication, state, and JSON

`storage login` is OAuth/OIDC device-code only. It requires `--homeserver`,
prints a verification URL and user code, and waits for browser approval. It
does not accept passwords, usernames, or a password-login mode.

The default profile (session and crypto state) is `~/.telecrypt-io/storage`.
Set `TELECRYPT_IO_STORAGE_HOME` for a separate account/device profile.

Every command accepts `--json` anywhere in the command line. Successful JSON
is written to stdout; errors use a non-zero exit code and JSON on stderr.

## Complete command tree

```text
telecrypt-io storage login --homeserver <url>
telecrypt-io storage whoami
telecrypt-io storage logout

telecrypt-io storage recovery setup
telecrypt-io storage recovery restore
telecrypt-io storage recovery restore --recovery-key-stdin

telecrypt-io storage folder create <name>
telecrypt-io storage folder list
telecrypt-io storage folder subfolder create <folderId> <name>
telecrypt-io storage folder subfolder list <folderId>
telecrypt-io storage folder join <folderId>
telecrypt-io storage folder share <folderId> <userId> [--role viewer|editor]
telecrypt-io storage folder members <folderId>
telecrypt-io storage folder unshare <folderId> <userId>
telecrypt-io storage folder rename <folderId> <name>
telecrypt-io storage folder delete <folderId>

telecrypt-io storage file upload <folderId> <path> [--name <name>]
telecrypt-io storage file list <folderId>
telecrypt-io storage file download <folderId> <fileId> <destPath>
telecrypt-io storage file rename <folderId> <fileId> <name>
telecrypt-io storage file delete <folderId> <fileId>
```

## Recovery Key safety

`recovery setup` prints a Recovery Key. Save it securely: it is required to
restore encryption keys on a new profile/device. Never put a Recovery Key in
argv, a shell command, process listings, or shell history. `recovery restore`
prompts securely by default. For non-interactive use, provide it only on stdin:

```bash
printf '%s\n' "$RECOVERY_KEY" | telecrypt-io storage recovery restore --recovery-key-stdin --json
```

Files are encrypted locally before upload. The server stores ciphertext; use
full Matrix user IDs (for example `@alice:homeserver.io`) when sharing folders.
